reportDate: Select the date this report was created so the team can clearly identify the reporting period.
projectName: Enter the name of the project being tested (for example: Project ABC).
projectType: Select the project type to help identify the testing scope.
updateNumber: Enter the sequence number of this report update (for example: #01, #02).
version: Enter the application or project version being tested (for example: v1.0.2).
buildLink: Provide a direct link to the latest build or artifact used for testing and verification.
totalIssues: Enter the total number of issues identified for this version.
totalIssuesLink: Provide a direct link to the filtered Jira issue list for this version.
majorIssues: Enter the number of high-severity issues, such as Critical or Blocker issues.
majorIssuesLink: Provide a direct link to high-severity or blocker issues in Jira.
licensedContent: Select the current verification status of licensed content included in this release.
licensedNote: Add any specific observations regarding licensed content verification.
audioCredits: Select the current verification status of the audio credits.
audioCreditsNote: Add any specific notes regarding the audio credits status.
resultStatus: Select the overall testing result, such as Pass, Fail, Blocked, or Needs Follow-up.
resultStatusNote: Provide additional context or reasons for the chosen overall result status.
testers: Select all testers who were involved in this testing cycle.
audioHighlights: Describe key findings or important updates specifically related to audio.
generalHighlights: Summarize the most important achievements or critical points from this period.
updateFollowUp: List any actions or items that require follow-up in the next report.
questions: List any unresolved questions or items that require stakeholder feedback.
milestones: Mention key project milestones achieved during this reporting period.
tvbLink: Provide a direct link to the TVB (Technical Verification Build) content.
tvbContent: Describe specific details or observations regarding the TVB content.
heatmapLink: Provide a URL to the heatmap visualization or report.
heatmapContent: Summarize findings or insights derived from the heatmap data.
platformsLink: Provide a link to platform-specific documentation or tracking tools.
platformsTracking: Detail how testing/tracking is being handled across different platforms.
subjectPreviews: Information about how email subjects are automatically generated based on reporting frequency.
emailPreview: Guidance on reviewing the final report layout before copying it to your email client.
issueLocation: Specify where the issue occurs (for example: Login Page, Settings Menu, or a specific in-game location).
issueObserver: Select who first observed the issue, such as a Player or an Internal Tester.
issueDescription: Provide a short and clear description of what happened.
impact: Describe how significantly the issue affects the user experience, functionality, or system.
expectedResult: Describe what should happen when the feature works correctly.
stepsToReproduce: Provide clear, step-by-step instructions that allow the issue to be reproduced consistently.
additionalNotes: Add any additional details, observations, conditions, or supporting information that may help with investigation.
bugReportOutput: Instructions for using the generated bug description, such as copying it directly into Jira.
jiraEmail: Enter the email address you use to sign in to Jira (for example: your.name@gameloft.com).
jiraApiToken:
How to Get Your Jira API Token

  1. Open gameloft.atlassian.net.
  2. Click your account icon in the top-right corner.
  3. Select Account settings.
  4. Open the Security tab.
  5. Find the API tokens section.
  6. Click Create and manage API tokens.
  7. Click Create API token.
  8. Enter a descriptive name, such as QAToolkit.
  9. Create the token and copy it to a secure location.

Important: Treat your API token like a password. Do not share it or store it in an unsecured location.
openWebUiApiKey:
How to Get Your AskAI API Key

  1. Open ask.ai.gameloft.org.
  2. Click your profile icon in the bottom-right corner.
  3. Select Settings, then scroll to the Account section.
  4. Find the API section and create a new API key.
  5. Copy the key (it starts with sk-) and paste it.

Important: Treat your API key like a password. Do not share it or store it in an unsecured location.
